description.narrative: Development and boost on micro-mobility, electromobility and last-mile transport in Peru from a sustainable mobility approach, with reference to the Netherlands private and public sector best practices. The project strengthens the collaboration and communication between these parties by:1. Implementing a baseline study describing context, actor mapping and normative framework on sustainable mobility and analysis of potential collaboration between private and public actors on sustainable mobility;2. Design of a road map, including concrete actions and suggestion on the set-up of potential collaboration between private and public actors on sustainable mobility;3. The establishment of a periodic working group on national level, consisting of public and private actors, to promote training, participation and the collaboration of actions in favour of micro-mobility, electromobility and last-mile transport in Peru, and;4. Presentation to communicate and promote opportunities which have been identified for bilateral collaboration on sustainable mobility.

comment.narrative: No real changes yet, but these are some of the regulations where the embassy can take action: ? It is necessary to improve the regulations, standards, regarding the behavior of micromobility users in Peru. The experience of the Netherlands is very useful because they have decades seeing how it is better to manage the movements of behaviors. ? Law Nº 30900 was enacted in 2019 to create the Urban Transport Authority for Urban Transportation for Lima and Callao (Autoridad de Transporte Urbano para Lima y Callao or ATU in Spanish). The ATU is responsible for the planning, organization, regulation, and supervision of urban public transport services in the metropolitan area of Lima and Callao. ATU has to approve the urban logistics plan for Lima and Callao (Directoral Resolution No. 021-2022-ATU/DIR). For this, the experiences of Amsterdam, Utrecht, among other cities, are important. ? Peru is currently developing a regulatory framework to implement electric charging infrastructure. Any national policy on electric transport exists up to date. Thus, Dutch expertise could enrich this blooming sector. Dutch Government actions such as researching, investing, subsidizing, and regulating electric transport could help the Peruvian Government to adjust best practices to the local context. ? The Peruvian National Government lacks a national last-mile logistics policy, while provinces lack proper local regulations. The Netherlands' support through its government and private companies could help the Peruvian Government develop better last-mile logistics policy and regulations.
